h1: The 6 Best Worx Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Worx Leaf Blowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Worx leaf blowers, cordless and Trivac 3-in-1, compared on airflow in CFM, format and price range so you can match yard size.
summary: The 780 CFM Worx Cordless is the strongest blower here, the 530 CFM is the balanced middle, and the Trivac 3-in-1 adds vacuum and mulching at 600 CFM. The 360 CFM cordless is the cheaper pick for small yards, and the 340 CFM backpack is the format outlier.
intro: Several Worx blowers share nearly identical names, so the number that actually separates them is airflow in CFM. Buying by name alone is the quickest way to end up with a 360 CFM unit when you needed 780.

We ranked six Worx blowers using the CFM, power type and format each listing states, and the price range each falls in. We reviewed spec sheets, not field performance, and where several listings share a name we tell them apart by airflow.

products.name: Worx Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The 780 CFM cordless is the most powerful Worx blower in this ranking.
products.description:
This cordless Worx blower lists 780 CFM of airflow, the highest of any pick here, and falls in the $100 to $200 range.

It leads because airflow is the one spec that decides how much yard a blower can clear. Next down the list, the 530 CFM model offers less than two thirds of that airflow in the same price range.

Buy it for larger yards or wet, heavy leaves. Our data does not give battery or run-time details, so confirm those on the listing.
pros: Same price range as weaker models
products.idealFor: Larger yards and heavy leaf cleanup.
products.skipIf: You only have a small patio.

products.name: WORX Trivac 3-in-1 Electric Leaf Blower/Leaf Vacuum/Leaf Mulcher
products.verdict: Blows, vacuums and mulches at 600 CFM for $50 to $100.
products.description:
The Trivac is an electric 3-in-1 that works as a blower, leaf vacuum and mulcher, listing 600 CFM of airflow. It costs $50 to $100.

It lands here since it does more than the cordless models, though it is electric rather than cordless. Against the 530 CFM cordless it has more airflow and a lower price, but gives up the freedom of no cord.

Best for a yard where you want to mulch leaves as you clear them. Check the listing for cord and bag details.
products.idealFor: Gardeners who want to mulch leaves.

products.name: WORX Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 530 CFM cordless for mid-sized yards.
products.description:
This WORX cordless blower lists 530 CFM and is priced from $100 to $200.

Where it sits comes down to the fact that the 780 CFM model costs the same and moves far more air, and the Trivac adds vacuum and mulching. It still beats the 410 CFM unit below on airflow.

Buy it for mid-sized yards if you can find it at a good price. Check battery details on the listing.
products.skipIf: A stronger model costs the same.

products.name: WORX Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 410 CFM cordless for tidy small and mid-sized lawns.
products.description:
This WORX cordless blower lists 410 CFM and is priced from $100 to $200.

The ordering here reflects that it offers less airflow than the 530 and 780 CFM models at the same price. It does edge out the 360 CFM unit below on airflow.

Choose it for light cleanup. Compare the 530 CFM model before buying.
products.skipIf: You want the best airflow per dollar.

products.name: WORX Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The cheaper 360 CFM cordless for decks and small yards.
products.description:
This WORX cordless blower lists 360 CFM and is priced from $50 to $100.

Its position follows from the fact that airflow trails every model above it, but it is the least expensive cordless here. That price gap is its main selling point against the 410 CFM model.

Buy it for a deck, driveway or small yard. Skip it for large lawns.

products.name: WORX Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 340 CFM backpack-format blower for longer sessions.
products.description:
This WORX unit is a backpack-format blower listing 340 CFM, priced from $200 to $500.

This slot reflects that it has the lowest airflow here at the highest price. The backpack format is its only differentiator against the handhelds.

Buy it if carrying weight on your back matters more than raw airflow. Otherwise a handheld gives more for less.
products.idealFor: Long cleanup sessions on your feet.
products.skipIf: You want the most airflow for the money.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is cubic feet per minute, the volume of air a blower moves. Higher CFM clears more leaves at once, especially wet ones. Find the figure in the listing title or bullets, since several Worx models share a name.
Cordless blowers run on a battery, so there is no cord but runtime is limited. Electric models run indefinitely but need an outlet and extension cord. Decide by yard size and outlet distance.
A 3-in-1 unit can blow, vacuum and mulch leaves. Mulching reduces bag volume. Check that the listing names the functions and includes the attachments.
Handheld blowers are lighter to store and cheaper. Backpack blowers move weight to your back for long sessions. Choose by how long you work at once.
Worx units here run from $50 to $500. A higher range does not always mean more airflow, so compare the CFM first.

faq.q: Why do several Worx blowers have the same name?
faq.a: Worx reuses the name across models. The CFM and listing number are what separate them.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Buying by name rather than CFM. Airflow here runs from 340 to 780 CFM.

faq.q: Is the Trivac worth it over a cordless model?
faq.a: If you want to mulch leaves, yes. It costs $50 to $100 but needs an outlet.

faq.q: Which blower is best for a small deck?
faq.a: The 360 CFM cordless is enough and the cheapest cordless here.

faq.q: How do I check battery details?
faq.a: Our data does not list battery specs, so read the listing before buying.

faq.q: Why is the backpack blower ranked last?
faq.a: It has the lowest airflow at 340 CFM and the highest price range.

finalTake: The 780 CFM cordless Worx is the best overall pick. The Trivac is the best choice if you want to mulch, and the 360 CFM cordless covers small spaces on a budget. Because model names overlap, always confirm the CFM on the listing.
